4875295_002a714a.text: The hippocampus is grossly comprised of five excitatory cell populations; namely, granule and mossy cells of the dentate gyrus (DG), and pyramidal cells of CA3, CA2, and CA1.
4875295_002a714a.section: Major Glutamatergic Cell Types in Hippocampal Subfields

4875295_7ffff871.text: The hippocampus contains five major populations of excitatory glutamatergic neurons distributed across distinct anatomical subfields (Cembrowski et al., 2016). These include granule cells and mossy cells in the dentate gyrus (DG), and pyramidal cells in the CA3, CA2, and CA1 regions (Cembrowski et al., 2016).
4875295_7ffff871.section: Major Glutamatergic Cell Types in Hippocampal Subfields

4875295_4a456257.text: we used next-generation RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) to produce a quantitative, whole genome characterization of gene expression for the major excitatory neuronal classes of the hippocampus; namely, granule cells and mossy cells of the dentate gyrus, and pyramidal cells of areas CA3, CA2, and CA1

4875295_8cb069d9.text: we profiled transcriptomes at both dorsal and ventral poles, producing a cell-class- and region-specific transcriptional description for these populations
